cars.generation: Original prewar Alvis Speed performance-road family
cars.variant: Speed 25 — 1937 National Motor Museum Charlesworth reference
cars.specification_market: Custodian’s own 1937 Charlesworth-bodied collection car is the selected reference. cars.summary: The Speed 25 is a landmark British sporting tourer, combining independent front suspension, an all-synchromesh gearbox and servo-assisted braking. Its documented fast-road character and advanced chassis make the Alvis Speed family an important prewar performance icon beyond prestige or rarity.

cars.specification_market: Actual English manufacturer brochure pages 2 and 4 rendered and read. It explicitly offers Model 710 Short to owner-drivers for touring, separately from racing use. The modern factory history dates the SSK family to 1928; the leaflet itself is undated, so that is programme context rather than a proven print date or pictured car’s build year. Use its rounded 7.1-litre class and stated road hardware, not conflicting exact-displacement/power figures, racing SSKL tune, Trossi special or a replica. No extra S/SS/SSK variant count is added.
cars.summary: The SSK is a foundational supercharged performance-car icon, bringing the short-chassis S-series’ competition-derived engineering to owner-driver touring. Its period road offering and enduring sporting identity establish a distinct family before the later 500 K already archived.

cars.generation: Original Model J production-road performance-GT family
cars.variant: Model J Tourster by Derham — 1931 Haynes Motor Museum reference
cars.specification_market: Haynes’ own 1931 Model J Tourster is the selected road reference. Treat its quoted output and brake description as the custodian’s collection-car account, not certification of untouched equipment or a measured universal specification. The separately read factory Model J technical pages establish core architecture and transmission. No supercharged SJ/SSJ output, prototype test car, Mormon Meteor racing tune, unverified speed, production total or celebrity-owner certainty is imported. One Model J family record is counted.
cars.summary: The Model J is a defining American performance-car icon: its twin-cam, four-valve engine and four-wheel hydraulic brakes brought exceptional engineering to the road. The documented Derham Tourster represents that influential family, whose significance extends beyond celebrity ownership and luxury coachwork.
